source.title_on_document: Generative AI and Creativity: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis

supplement.where: GitHub repository https://github.com/SM2982/Meta-Analysis-LLMs-Creativity.git (p. 2, footnote 1; p. 22, Data Availability)
supplement.holds: Extracted study database, effect-size conversion formulas, meta-regression results, risk-of-bias and publication-bias results, construct-level subgroup analyses, and code (pp. 3, 5-6)

paper_design_summary: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird, Hedges' g) of 28 between-subject studies (127 effect sizes, 8,214 participants) found in Web of Science, SSRN, and arXiv up to May 2, 2025. It pools three comparisons: GenAI output versus human output (RQ1), creativity of humans with versus without GenAI support (RQ2a), and diversity of ideas of humans with versus without GenAI support (RQ2b).

assignment.prereg_locator: p. 22, Review Protocol: "No review protocol was preregistered for this study."

participants.who: Participants of 28 included studies: academia (85 of 127 effect sizes), laypeople (14), business (9), and 19 studies with undisclosed or mixed backgrounds. RQ1 draws on 4,582 participants, RQ2a on 2,798, RQ2b on 1,017.
participants.quote: and eventually identified 𝑛= 28 studies with empirical results (𝑚= 8214 participants).

ai_tool.name_model: Various text-to-text models (all included studies coded T2T in Table 2, p. 7); GPT-4 (37 of 127 effect sizes) and GPT-3.5 (25) most frequent (p. 8, Section 3.1)
ai_tool.how_used: Varies across included studies (Table 1, p. 5; Table 2, p. 7).

task.description: Mixed across studies: creative writing (48 of 127 effect sizes), creative problem solving (25), alternate uses test (12), business ideation (fewer than 15 percent), plus consequences task, divergent association task, forward flow (p. 8, Section 3.1; Table 1, p. 5).

synthesis.search_end: May 2, 2025 (Web of Science, SSRN, arXiv; English, past five years)
synthesis.inclusion: Between-subject experiments comparing (a) creativity of humans versus GenAI or (b) creativity of humans with versus without GenAI support; statistics sufficient for Hedges' g (or raw data with documented code); creativity measured on an established dimension such as novelty, originality, or diversity (p. 3). Screening by one person (first author); two studies added manually (pp. 2-3).

pooled.comparison: RQ2a: humans with GenAI vs humans alone, creativity (21 effect sizes, m = 2798)
pooled.what_it_standardizes: Hedges' g from reported Cohen's d or converted from t, F, means and SDs (p. 5); measures vary across included studies. The review prioritized expert evaluations over self-assessments and overall creativity over originality or novelty (p. 5, Section 2.2).
pooled.locator: p. 5, Sections 2.2-2.3; p. 11, Section 3.3; p. 12, Fig. 4; p. 15, Table 3

pooled.comparison: RQ2b: humans with GenAI vs humans alone, diversity of ideas (6 effect sizes from 4 studies, m = 1017)
pooled.what_it_standardizes: Hedges' g of each study's diversity measure. Six effect sizes from four studies: CD01 Doshi and Hauser [16], CD02 Doshi, Chai, and Troebinger [15], CD03 Ismayilzada et al. [31], and CD04 Chen and Chan [9]. Table 2 lists cosine similarity for CD01/CD02 and a creativity scale for CD03/CD04; these are the review's classifications, not independently verified primary-study measures. The pooled analysis does not specify an embedding model or which outputs were compared. Random-effects pooling (DerSimonian-Laird); negative g means less diverse ideas with GenAI. Egger's test and trim-and-fill were not run because of the number of studies.
pooled.locator: p. 5, Section 2.3; p. 7, Table 2 (CD01-CD04); p. 13, Section 3.4; p. 14, Fig. 6 and Section 3.4.2; p. 15, Table 3; pp. 18-19, references [9], [15], [16], [31]

eligibility.reason: Systematic review and meta-analysis with no original participant experiment (pp. 2-5, Sections 2.1-2.3). The 8,214 participants belong to the 28 included publications (p. 2, Section 1; p. 3, Section 2.1); they are not an original trial sample satisfying the core criteria. All analyses use effect-size estimates (p. 8, Section 3). Its RQ2a and RQ2b studies (p. 7, Table 2) are leads for primary experiments to screen separately. The paper remains synthesis context evidence under creativity-codebook.md, Section 3.

one_line_finding: Across 28 studies (8,214 participants), GenAI output matched human output (g = -0.048, 95% CI [-0.257, 0.161]), humans with GenAI were more creative than humans without (g = 0.273, 95% CI [0.018, 0.528], 21 effect sizes), and their ideas were less diverse (g = -0.863, 95% CI [-1.328, -0.398], 6 effect sizes from 4 studies) (pp. 8, 11, 13; Table 3, p. 15).
open_questions: Table 2 (p. 7) lists Ismayilzada et al. [31] (story generation by humans and LLMs) as diversity study CD03, though its title suggests an AI-versus-human comparison rather than humans with versus without AI.
Section 2.3 (p. 5) says one effect size per experiment, yet the analyses use 127 effect sizes from 28 studies, several per study (p. 8).
notes: Only arXiv v1 seen. Table 3 caption (p. 15) says a check mark indicates p < 0.001, but RQ2a is marked with a check at p = 0.036 and one star. Inclusion required a between-subject design; randomization is not stated as a criterion. Pooled estimates, effect-size counts, heterogeneity and sensitivity results are recorded in synthesis.pooled; no primary-study outcomes are coded for this review (creativity-codebook.md, Section 3, Synthesis; p. 8, Section 3).
